name: GA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Nikema Williams running for reelection
Minimal Republican funding or outside support
model.rationale: Atlanta-based GA-05 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, and incumbent Nikema Williams is running with a solid cash advantage while her opponent has shown no measurable fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win near certain, so the fundamentals-based margin stands.
model.watch: Any surprise polling or a major outside-spending intervention for the Republican challenger would be the only realistic sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nikema Williams, the Democratic incumbent in this Atlanta-based district, is seeking another term against Republican John Oscar Salvesen. The seat is among the most heavily Democratic in the nation, with a partisan lean of roughly D+36, and no expert rating organizations list the race as competitive. Williams has raised about $600,000, while her opponent's fundraising is not reported, suggesting little serious Republican investment here.

Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability at 99 percent, and no general-election polling exists, which is typical for races this lopsided. The forecast expects Williams to win by a wide, roughly thirty-point margin, with modest uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any evidence of a competitive race.
